title: Your First Weekend at Lewis & Clark College, Shared as Cards
description: A flexible Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning campus landmarks, sharing a meal, seeing art, finding a quiet reset, and exploring nearby Tryon Creek.

cards.title: Start at the Manor
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Learn the campus anchor
cards.notes: Begin outside Frank Manor House, then use its east-facing terrace as your reference point for the historic campus core.
cards.short_summary: Orient yourself around the former Fir Acres estate’s central building.
cards.evidence_claim: Frank Manor House is a 35-room Tudor-style mansion built in 1924–25 and now serves as Lewis & Clark’s administrative core.
cards.access_notes: The cited page documents current administrative uses; it does not promise public interior access, so treat this as an exterior orientation stop.

cards.title: Find the Campus Bronze
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Add one precise landmark
cards.notes: Walk southeast of Frank Manor House and locate Glenna Goodacre’s seven-foot bronze; use it to practice navigating by named features.
cards.short_summary: Meet a permanent artwork with a clearly documented campus location.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark’s seven-foot Sacagawea and Jean Baptiste bronze by Glenna Goodacre is permanently installed southeast of Frank Manor House.
cards.access_notes: The sculpture is permanently installed outdoors southeast of Frank Manor House; the source lists no visiting hours.

cards.title: Make Dinner the Meet-Up
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Share an easy gathering point
cards.notes: Choose Fields as the group rendezvous, confirm the day’s service before leaving, and decide together where to sit after everyone arrives.
cards.short_summary: Use the main undergraduate dining hall as a simple first-night anchor.
cards.evidence_claim: Fields Dining Room is Lewis & Clark’s main undergraduate dining hall and serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
cards.access_notes: Located in Fowler Student Center. Check the linked dining information for current service details; the page does not state exact hours.

cards.title: Learn Your Evening Base
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Preview a future study stop
cards.notes: Bring your L&C ID, identify the entrances and main-floor services, and note where you could regroup for a quieter evening later.
cards.short_summary: Get familiar with the library before coursework makes the visit urgent.
cards.evidence_claim: Since March 30, 2026, Watzek Library access from 6 p.m. to midnight Sunday through Thursday has been limited to the Lewis & Clark community and requires an L&C ID card.
cards.access_notes: Carry an L&C ID for entry from 6 p.m. to midnight Sunday–Thursday. Verify current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Garden Terraces
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Trace the estate landscape
cards.notes: Start near Frank Manor House and follow the four descending terraces, pausing where paths and water features reveal the garden’s layout.
cards.short_summary: Read the historic estate through its surviving formal garden structure.
cards.evidence_claim: The Edna Holmes estate gardens comprise four terraces descending east from Frank Manor House toward the former rose garden and Mount Hood view.
cards.access_notes: The source describes the grounds but gives no public hours; remain on open paths and follow posted campus restrictions.

cards.entity_name: Ronna and Eric Hoffman Gallery of Contemporary Art
cards.title: See What’s on the Walls
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Make room for contemporary art
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition before walking over, then give each person time to choose one work to discuss outside afterward.
cards.short_summary: Turn a free gallery visit into an easy first-weekend conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hoffman Gallery is free and open to the public daily from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Ronna and Eric Hoffman Gallery of Contemporary Art
cards.access_notes: Open daily 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; check the official page for exhibition dates or temporary changes before visiting.

cards.title: Follow Sound into the Trees
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Explore an outdoor art space
cards.notes: Look behind Fields Center for the speaker-lined path, listen only when programming is active, and avoid handling installed equipment.
cards.short_summary: Encounter the wooded campus as a setting for spatial sound work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Experimental Art Research Forest is a 16-channel speaker array behind Fields Center for the Visual Arts used for scheduled sound-based programming.
cards.source_title: Making (Sound) Waves in the EAR Forest
cards.access_notes: Programming is scheduled rather than continuous. Use open paths and check the college calendar before expecting an active sound work.

cards.title: Map the Student Hub
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Locate practical resources
cards.notes: Walk each public level and note the bookstore, dining areas, and College Outdoors office so future errands begin with a known route.
cards.short_summary: Learn where several everyday student services converge.
cards.evidence_claim: Fowler Student Center contains Fields Dining Room, the Trail Room, the bookstore, College Outdoors, and Student Engagement facilities.
cards.access_notes: Individual offices, shops, and dining venues set their own access and service times; verify them before planning a specific errand.

cards.title: Take a Quiet Sunday Pause
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Reset before the week
cards.notes: Stop for reflection, rest, or contemplation, keep the shared room quiet, and leave time to look for posted events before departing.
cards.short_summary: Use a documented daily reflection space for a calm weekend reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark’s undergraduate catalog states that Agnes Flanagan Chapel is available daily for reflection, prayer, rest, and contemplation.
cards.source_title: Student Services, Resources, and Programs - Undergraduate Catalog
cards.access_notes: Available daily for reflection, prayer, rest, and contemplation; scheduled services or events may affect use of the room.

cards.title: Close with a Forest Walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Explore beyond campus
cards.notes: Check conditions, choose a signed trail that fits the group, carry water, and allow extra time because wet-weather surfaces can be muddy.
cards.short_summary: Finish the weekend on a maintained trail in Portland’s state natural area.
cards.evidence_claim: Tryon Creek State Natural Area has eight miles of hiking trails maintained for year-round use, plus a 0.3-mile fully paved Trillium Trail.
cards.access_notes: May–August park hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; the Nature Center is open daily 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Day-use parking requires a permit.
